name: Monstera
wateringInstructions: Water thoroughly once every 7 days. Allow top 2 inches of soil to dry out between waterings.
advantages: Excellent air purifier by absorbing volatile chemical elements
Highly aesthetic addition to any indoor setup with signature leaf holes
Easy to propagate from stem cuttings
disadvantages: Mildly toxic to cats and dogs if ingested
Requires significant floor space as it matures
careTips: Place in bright to medium indirect sunlight.
Maintain room humidity above 50% for optimal leaf splits.
Wipe the large leaves with a damp cloth occasionally to clear dust.
uses: Excellent air purifier by absorbing volatile chemical elements
Highly aesthetic addition to any indoor setup with signature leaf holes

name: Aloe Vera
wateringInstructions: Water deeply every 14 days, ensuring complete soil dryness between cycles.
advantages: Soothes sunburns, minor cuts, and skin irritations with natural gel
Highly drought-tolerant, extremely hard to kill
Produces offsets or 'pups' easily for sharing
disadvantages: Prone to root rot if overwatered or kept in stagnant clay soil
Sharp, spiky leaf margins require careful placement away from narrow corridors
careTips: Requires plenty of bright direct sunlight (minimum 6 hours daily).
Always use a well-draining cactus or succulent soil mix.
Grow in terracotta pots which allow moisture to wick away quickly.
uses: Soothes sunburns, minor cuts, and skin irritations with natural gel

name: Snake Plant
wateringInstructions: Water sparingly every 21 days. Highly sensitive to wet soil, err on the side of dryness.
advantages: Extremely hardy and thrives under high neglect
Produces oxygen at night, making it ideal for bedroom placement
Tolerates low light environments exceptionally well
disadvantages: Toxic to pets if chewed or swallowed
Slow growth rate compared to other tropicals
careTips: Keep in moderate to indirect low light conditions.
Do not water the center rosette directly; water around the soil base.
Repot only when the strong roots begin cracking the container.
uses: Produces oxygen at night, making it ideal for bedroom placement

name: Peace Lily
wateringInstructions: Water every 5 days. Keep soil consistently moist but never soggy. Drops leaves when thirsty.
advantages: Striking white spade-like blooms throughout the year
Actively cleans indoor toxins like benzene and formaldehyde
Foliage acts as an excellent organic indicator of watering needs
disadvantages: Contains calcium oxalate crystals, toxic to pets and children
Sensitive to high chlorine or fluoride in municipal tap water
careTips: Thrives in medium to low indirect light; direct sun burns leaves.
If possible, water with filtered, distilled, or rainwater.
Mist leaves occasionally to mimic its native tropical rainforest environment.
uses: Actively cleans indoor toxins like benzene and formaldehyde

name: Lavender
wateringInstructions: Water every 10 days until established, then reduce watering. Thrives in dry, hot soil.
advantages: Produces highly soothing fragrance proven to reduce anxiety
Attracts key beneficial pollinators like honeybees and butterflies
Beautiful purple spikes that can be harvested and dried
disadvantages: Struggles indoors due to high humidity and lack of intense sunlight
Requires yearly pruning to prevent woody, leggy growth
careTips: Plant in full outdoor sun (at least 8 hours of direct light).
Requires alkaline, sandy, or gravel-rich soil with super drainage.
Prune about one-third of the green growth in early spring.
uses: Produces highly soothing fragrance proven to reduce anxiety

name: Giant Milkweed
wateringInstructions: Water sparingly. Thrives in dry, sandy soil and requires full sun exposure.
advantages: Attracts monarch butterflies and other pollinators
disadvantages: Milky sap is highly toxic to humans and pets
Can become invasive if left unmanaged
careTips: Do not overwater; ensure soil drains completely.
Wear gloves when handling to avoid irritation from the sap.
